title: Explaining why Sweden’s World Cup training base is crumbling around them: ‘What the hell happened?’
content:
Sweden’s World Cup training in Frisco, Texas had a strange backdrop on Wednesday.

Graham Potter’s players were preparing for their final World Cup group game against Japan on Thursday, beneath what looked like a collapsed grandstand and a great pile of debris.

It confused the players, too, including midfielder Besfort Zeneli, who was asked about the pile of rubble by the travelling Swedish media.

“I just thought, ‘What happened?’ As far as I know, there wasn’t a storm,” he said, via Aftonbladet.

He was right: there was no storm — nor was anybody hurt, and there was no impact on the training schedule or the usability of the pitch.

The Toyota Stadium, which is normally home to MLS side FC Dallas and the UFL franchise the Dallas Renegades, is currently undergoing a $182 million renovation project.

The works are due to be completed in 2028 and are continuing around World Cup training sessions, but while the demolition of the grandstand and press box were planned — there was a problem.

Stefan Pettersson, Sweden’s team manager, confirmed to Aftonbladet on Wednesday that he had been given prior warning of the issue, that the team’s ability to use the facilities had been completely unaffected, and that nobody had been hurt.

“They were supposed to demolish something and it looks like it fell in the wrong direction,” Pettersson said. “Luckily, no one was hurt. They probably detonated it and then something went wrong.

“The players were a bit wide-eyed when they arrived. They said, ‘Oh, what the hell happened?’ when they came and saw this. They didn’t know anything about it before.”

Having won their first game 5-1 against Tunisia, the Swedes then lost by the same scoreline against the Netherlands on the second matchday.

It leaves them in third place in Group F, needing a win against Japan in Arlington to guarantee a place in the knockout rounds.

An FC Dallas spokesperson told The Athletic: “The activity observed near FC Dallas Stadium occurred before Sweden’s training session and was part of a planned and controlled demolition within an active construction zone. The work was conducted using a pull-down demolition method and did not involve explosives. Training proceeded as scheduled, and Sweden completed its session as planned.”
